newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end off amid EMU delay speculation.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end off amid EMU delay speculation.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Austrian bonds tracked lower with the German Bund future, weighed down by weak U.S. trends and speculation about a delay in European Economic and Monetary Union, and traders predicted further losses.
"We are higher than we were at the start, but I think there is still downside potential," said one trader.
Stronger-than expected U.S. housing start figures led to early losses in the U.S. market but treasuries regained ground later in the session through short-covering.
* 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 steady at 99.55 to yield 5.82 pct (5.68) in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 98.26/36 to yield 5.86/85.
* Latest five-year 4.375 bond maturing February 2002 closed up 45 bps at 98.85 in bourse trade to yield 4.80 pct (4.69), quoted post-market at 97.76/97.86 to yield 4.82/4.80 percent.
* AGB future down 49 bps at 107.30 on turnover of 2,037 lots.
* 10-year spread over Germany steady at minus five bps, five-year spread down one at nine bps.
* Money market rates mixed with three-month VIBOR higher at 3.350 and overnight money at 3.08/3.33. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
